glossary.definition: After user consent, token exchange mints a delegated token: sub is the USER, act={sub: agent} names the actor. Every action traces back to a real human.

glossary.term: One mock PDP behind every wired track
glossary.definition: A single decision engine answers every wired use case: token checks, then the gateway chain check (actor allow-list, upstream audiences), then the policy (directory groups, tier ceilings, premium-only tools), then the obligation layer (amount bands and approval tools pause the call instead of denying it). The catalog tracks are framing over the same contract; all values are mock.
The policy reads directory groups on EVERY decision: outside the required group is denied regardless of scopes, and the premium group EXPANDS capability (restricted tools + a $50000 ceiling).

Bands and approval tools return OBLIGATIONS, not denials: the agent pauses, the human resolves a consent/MFA/CIBA challenge, and a call-bound receipt re-evaluates the SAME call. An approval is never an MFA.

Two RFC 8693 exchanges: the user consents and the generalist agent acts for them, then the generalist hands off and the specialist acts via it, so the token carries act={specialist, act:{generalist}} with the scope narrowed at each hop. The gateway routes the call only when the SPECIALIST is in the Agent Card registry; no bearer at all is a real 401.

sources.title: RFC 8693: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
sources.use: The act claim and the delegated-token shape behind the whole catalog.

cards.label: Scenario 1: UC1: consent mints act={agent} — the balance read permits
cards.description: One consent, one delegated token: sub is the user, act={demo-agent} names the actor. Every action traces to a real human.

cards.label: Scenario 2: UC9: not in the required group — denied regardless of scopes
cards.description: The policy reads directory groups on EVERY decision. No group, no access — the token’s scopes cannot override it.

cards.label: Scenario 3: UC9A: flip the directory entry — the very next call moves
cards.description: Revoke the privileged group and the SAME call denies — no code change, no cache, no re-login.

cards.label: Scenario 4: UC21: Standard tier cannot invoke the premium wire
cards.description: Positive least privilege: premium-only tools are listed in policy, never implied by scopes.

cards.label: Scenario 5: UC21: promote to Premium — the tool unlocks (then HITL pauses)
cards.description: Promotion first unlocks the tool (tier_tool_not_allowed is gone), then the HITL layer pauses it for approval — bands stack with groups, policy-driven, not hard-coded.

cards.label: Scenario 6: UC21: $60000 exceeds even the Premium ceiling
cards.description: Tiers cap amounts: Premium ceiling $50000, Standard $2000. Amounts are policy bands, not tool arguments.

cards.label: Scenario 7: UC6: an unknown agent is refused at the gateway
cards.description: Authorization keys on WHO is acting: the actor allow-list refuses an unregistered agent before any policy runs.

cards.label: Scenario 8: UC32: a token aimed at an upstream MCP is refused
cards.description: An audience is a destination: a token minted for an upstream MCP server is never accepted downstream.

cards.label: Scenario 9: UC7: MFA step-up — the agent pauses, the human completes MFA
cards.description: Mid-band ($500-$100000): consent + MFA. The agent PAUSES — it cannot self-approve. The receipt (MfaVerified) re-evaluates the SAME call.

cards.label: Scenario 10: UC8: HITL approval — an approval is never an MFA
cards.description: Human-approval tools always pause the agent, whatever the amount. Only a verified, call-bound HitlApproved receipt moves it.

cards.label: Scenario 11: UC22: CIBA — out-of-band approval on the user’s device
cards.description: An agent has no browser in which to prompt: the backend calls bc-authorize and the user approves out-of-band; the receipt (CibaApproved) re-evaluates the call.

cards.label: Browse the 87-use-case catalog
cards.description: Every use case from the AI-DEMO2 dashboard, grouped by track. The foundations, controls and HITL scenarios and the A2A panel run against the mock PDP; the attacks, learn, tools, nhi and demo tracks are catalog entries with their expected outcome, not yet wired.

cards.label: Build the A2A hand-off chain
cards.description: Two exchanges build act={specialist, act:{generalist}} with the scope narrowed per hop (UC2, UC2.5); register or revoke a specialist and the next call moves (UC2.6); no bearer is a real 401 (UC2.7).

cards.label: Flip the directory live
cards.description: Revoke the privileged group live; the SAME call flips on the next run — groups are read on EVERY decision.

cards.label: Doctor and health
cards.description: Preflight checks and the demo-health/1 endpoint.
